Owner Takes His Chevy Corvette to a Tuner, Drives Home With 1,000 Horsepower
12 photos
Photo: Late Model Racecraft | YouTube
When stock is no longer enough, dialing up your car is the ultimate way to make the owner fall in love with it over again. This is the story of this 2024 Chevrolet Corvette Z06. The owner dropped it off at a tuning shop and, a few weeks later, drove home in a 1,000-horsepower supercar.
The owner, Chris V., has had enough of stock. It just didn’t cut it for him anymore. So he drove straight to a tuner in Houston, Texas, and asked the experts to take his sports car to the next level. But what does "next level" actually mean?
In stock form, the naturally aspirated 5.5-liter flat-plane crank LT6 V8 pushes out, the 5.5-liter flat-plane crank LT6 V8 with naturally aspirated firepower power pushed out 670 horsepower (680 metric horsepower) and 460 pound-feet (623 Newton meters) of torque.
That is what made the Chevrolet Corvette Z06 rocket from 0 to 60 mph (0 to 97 kph) in just 2.6 seconds, run the quarter mile in 10.5 seconds with a trap speed of 131 mph (210 kph), and max out at 195 mph (314 kph).
Photo: Late Model Racecraft | YouTube Still craving more power, the owner, Chris, turned to Late Model Racecraft . He had already dialed it up, and the car baselined at around 600 rear-wheel horsepower on the dyno when running on E85. Long story short, LMR bolted a pair of turbos into the engine bay. The car now makes an additional 213 rear-wheel horsepower on 93-octane pump gas.
That brings the total to over 810 wheel horsepower, which translates to roughly 1,000 horsepower at the crank. It is a Mirror Image Precision ball-bearing turbo system. Coming out of the turbos, a short exhaust roars out all the drama of the V8 that powers the Corvette, popping and banging wildly on both full load and downshifts.
A heat exchanger runs coolant through it on both sides to keep temperature under control. Full ECM and TCM tune are part of the LMR Stage 1 Twin Turbo Package to upgrade power delivery on 93 octane, while maintaining factory-like drivability and reliability.
Steven Fereday from Late Model Racecraft takes the car for a spin to make sure he delivers a reliable build. In Sport mode, with traction control off, it spins the tires, but the driver had better keep it on when trying to win "races" from stoplight to stoplight. For more grip, a set of sticky Toyos on the rear axle would be a better option.
Photo: Late Model Racecraft | YouTube Back in Touring Mode, the car turns back to stock behavior. When Chris V. comes to pick up his car, the smile on his face says it all. It looks like he will be happy with his dialed-up C8 Corvette Z06 for a while. When he has had enough, there is always the Corvette ZR1X with 1,250 horsepower. However, that’s double the price of the Z06!

Blue Ford Mustang GTD Suddenly Becomes a Street Monster, Albeit Only Across Imagination Land, Sadly
9 photos
Photo: rostislav_prokop / Instagram
As far as the Ford Motor Company is concerned, they would love nothing more than fully directing our attention toward the upcoming introduction of their all-new 2027 Ford Fathom, the ‘game-changing’ electric pickup that costs less than $30k. Alas, enthusiasts have other plans.
The Blue Oval has continued its teaser campaign for the upcoming 2027 Fathom with a recent post describing the truck’s bidirectional charging function, which is coming with 10 kW of power and some caveats. More importantly, though, the company has let slip the Fathom’s exact starting MSRP: $28,350.
On the other hand, folks want nothing to do with EVs and instead focus on things that have V8s under the hood – like the Ford Mustang Dark Horse or the recent rumor about a new hypercar featuring a 5.4-liter V8 redlining at 9,000 rpm. As it turns out, it’s not a Boss Mustang coming from around the corner, and instead the news is about Ford’s all-new Le Mans hypercar developed for the 2027 FIA World Endurance Championship (WEC) Hypercar program.
Anyway, even the members of the imaginative guild of digital car content creators have stopped dwelling across the parallel universes of vehicular CGI to take a look at the S650 Ford Mustang lately. For example, Czech Republic-based virtual artist Rostislav Prokop, known as " rostislav_prokop " on social media, continues his thunderous dream ride periplus with a Mustang GTD that would make even Ford blush a little.
His ‘street monster’ unofficial, hypothetical design project for the mighty S650 Ford Mustang GTD is “American muscle taken to the extreme,” with a vision for an ultra-widebody GTD aerodynamic kit, “a striking blue-and-red color combination, and aggressive street-focused proportions.” This version of the legal race car also rides on deep-dish, three-piece forged Rotiform wheels featuring carbon fiber lips — “a combination of precision, attitude, and pure performance-inspired design.”
The idea comes with things like RTR-inspired front grille LED elements, a lowered suspension setup, and new oval dual exhausts around the back – so it’s going to be quite easy to differentiate from the real Ford Mustang GTD. As for the powertrain, the pixel master doesn’t say anything about additional changes, meaning it’s the same 815-hp 5.2-liter supercharged V8.
By the way, the Ford Mustang GTD has been around since the summer of 2023 as a street-version of Blu Oval’s FIA Group GT3 race car and with the moniker an abbreviation of the Grand Touring Daytona class, which raced in the IMSA SportsCar Championship. The predator-equipped supercar was the first American car that lapped the infamous Nürburgring Nordschleife in less than seven minutes back in late 2024.
It beat its own record in May 2025, but in July 2025 General Motors quickly sent the 2026 Chevrolet Corvette ZR1 and ZR1X to beat its time, to which Ford CEO Jim Farley replied with “game on” after congratulating them. So, in April 2026, the Ford Mustang GTD once again went to the Green Hell, this time with the new Mustang GTD Competition version, and established the current reigning lap time of 6:40.835 for American cars. 2026 SEMA Show • 2028 Mitsubishi Outlander Diamond Trail Edition: How Does It Compare to Other Adventure Crossovers?
Dodge Challenger Hellcat Drags Plymouth Barracuda in New vs. Old School Clash, It's Over In 10.31s
13 photos
Photo: Wheels / YouTube
The videographer behind the " Wheels " channel on YouTube is a big fan of Mission Raceway Park, and they present us with a rivalry of the Mopar variety between a recently-retired Dodge Challenger SRT Hellcat and the long-ago-retired third-gen Plymouth ‘Cuda. Yep, it’s ‘new versus old school’ all over again.
The videographer behind the ' Wheels ' channel on YouTube recently took a detour around BMP – Bradenton Motorsports Park in Florida - for the FL2K competition, showing us cool things like a white C8 Chevrolet Corvette ZR1 battling the slightly older S550 Ford Mustang Shelby GT500 among other feisty skirmishes. But now they’re back at MRP.
Also known as Thunder by the River , MRP is a cool auto racing facility located in Mission, British Columbia, Canada, hosting an NHRA-sanctioned dragstrip of the quarter-mile variety along with a nine-turn road course and also a motocross track. It’s home to a variety of clashes because it’s open to anyone, and the videographer’s catches from here never disappoint.
But let’s meet the new and old contestants first. In the right lane resides a matte black Dodge Challenger SRT Hellcat, which isn’t alive anymore since production ended in December 2023, but of course it’s much newer than the gray third-generation Plymouth Barracuda from the early 1970s. The latter was probably restored and enhanced for this encounter, but let’s see if it can cope with the supercharged 6.2-liter Hemi V8’s modern oomph.
Well, as it turns out, the ‘Cuda driver pushed the Plymouth hard right off the start, thus nailing a slightly better launch off the line – the Challenger SRT Hellcat and its siblings are notoriously finicky during the start sequence. As such, it looked like it could pull a surprise out of the magician’s hat, but it was merely an impression.
Once the Hellcat got going, the Dodge was relentless in its pursuit and quickly took over the race to post a very nice victory: 10.31s at almost 133 mph versus a meager 12.57s at a much lower trap speed of 106 mph. But wait, as there is more of the ‘new versus old’ variety, with a second clash showcasing another ‘fraternal’ battle featuring a brand-new C8 Chevrolet Corvette E-Ray performance hybrid sports car and a derelict-looking Chevrolet Nova muscle car.
The latter was rolling coal through its hood exhaust in a bid to intimidate the electrified mid-engine sports car or at least impair the driver’s visibility – but it was all for nothing. Instead, the AWD C8 took off like a dart and left the Nova in a cloud of smoke, winning the skirmish with a 10.75s pass. The older Chevy actually posted a perfect 10s pass, but since the C8 crossed the finish line first, it was a futile attempt – all for show, not for glory.

Borderlands Mexico is a weekly rundown of developments in the world of United States-Mexico cross-border trucking and trade. This week in Borderlands Mexico: Cabotage enforcements threatening cross-border trucking; Nuevo León slashes Colombia Bridge toll fees 50% to boost cross-border trucking; and Walmart plans $400M distribution center near San Antonio, creating 425 jobs.
Cabotage enforcements threatening cross-border trucking
JACKSONVILLE, Fla. — Knight-Swift Transportation CEO Adam Miller said stepped-up enforcement of U.S. cabotage restrictions is creating new challenges for Mexican truck drivers and could further tighten cross-border trucking capacity .
Speaking in an interview with FreightWaves on Tuesday at the second annual WEX OTR Summit in Jacksonville, Miller said U.S. authorities have intensified scrutiny of Mexican drivers operating across the border, including reviewing potential cabotage violations involving their previous employers.
“We’re seeing the enforcement really ramp up on cabotage,” Miller said.
Cabotage generally refers to domestic transportation between two points within a country by a foreign carrier, an activity subject to restrictions under U.S. law.
Miller said Knight-Swift (NYSE: KNX ), which operates in Mexico through its TransMex subsidiary, has observed cases in which drivers faced visa revocations over alleged violations committed while working for other carriers.
“I’ve seen them take visas away from drivers from really a previous carrier, not even cabotage with our trucks, with our company,” Miller said.
Knight-Swift Transportation is one of the largest full truckload carriers in the U.S., operating a massive fleet of more than 26,000 tractors, 96,000 trailers and 28,000 employees. Nogales, Mexico-based TransMex operates over 1,100 tractor-trailers and more than 3,000 trailers.
Miller said Knight-Swift maintains strict compliance policies governing its cross-border operations, but the increased scrutiny could discourage some Mexican drivers from entering the United States.
“I do feel like that type of capacity is going to get a little bit tighter as enforcement ramps up,” Miller said.
The CEO’s comments come amid growing concerns among Mexican trucking companies over U.S. enforcement of cabotage restrictions and the potential loss of drivers authorized to transport international freight.
Despite the enforcement challenges, Miller said he remains optimistic about the long-term growth of U.S.-Mexico freight transportation.
“I think long term I think Mexico is going to play a bigger role,” Miller said. “I think you’ll see more opportunities because of the nearshoring.”
However, he cautioned that uncertainty surrounding tariffs and trade policy could affect freight volumes and investment decisions.
“Tariffs are a big unknown,” Miller said.
Knight-Swift transports significant automotive freight across the border, and Miller said some customers have adjusted their transportation strategies in response to tariff developments.
“Our customer strategies are changing as the tariff situation develops,” he said.
Nuevo León slashes Colombia Bridge toll fees 50% to boost cross-border trucking
The Mexican state of Nuevo León announced a 50% reduction in state-imposed toll charges for commercial trucks traveling to the Colombia-Solidarity International Bridge, a move aimed at lowering transportation costs and boosting exports to the U.S.
The reduction applies to an additional state toll collected about 500 meters before the existing bridge tollbooth on the Mexican side of the border. The fee was introduced April 14, 2025, under Nuevo León Gov. Samuel García’s administration.
The discount does not affect tolls collected by the city of Laredo, Texas.
The initiative is designed to make the Colombia crossing more competitive for freight shipments and encourage logistics companies to route additional commercial traffic through the port of entry.
“By working together to reduce tolls and fees, we can help lower transportation costs, support businesses, and strengthen the movement of goods through our region,” Treviño said, according to the Laredo Morning Times .
The Colombia-Solidarity International Bridge connects Nuevo León with the Laredo area and serves as an alternative route for cross-border truck shipments moving between Mexico and the U.S.
Walmart plans $400M distribution center near San Antonio, creating 425 jobs
Walmart (Nasdaq: WMT ) is planning a $400 million distribution center in Cibolo, Texas, northeast of San Antonio, according to the San Antonio Express-News .
The proposed facility, identified as “Project Theo,” will include a 712,500-square-foot warehouse and a connected 31,933-square-foot office building on approximately 126 acres at 3641 S. Santa Clara Road, according to a filing with the Texas Department of Licensing and Regulation.
Construction is scheduled to begin in February 2027, with completion expected in August 2029.
The project is expected to create at least 425 full-time jobs paying above the San Antonio metropolitan area’s median salary.
Cibolo officials previously approved an incentive package valued at approximately $32.5 million to attract the development, including a 75% property tax abatement for 10 years.
City officials have described the proposed facility as a next-generation distribution center that will use robotics, advanced warehouse equipment and employees to manage automated operations.
The development would expand Walmart’s distribution footprint along the Interstate 35 and Interstate 10 corridors, major freight arteries connecting San Antonio, Austin and other Texas markets.

"Cat-eye" GMT800 Chevrolet Silverado Gets Rendered With ZR1 Treatment, Would Be Great With 1,064 HP
7 photos
Photo: abimelecdesign / Instagram
General Motors has diligently taken care of the full-size pickup truck series this year. Both the regular Chevy Silverado and GMC Sierra 1500, but also the HD models, of course. There’s no discrimination, which is a good thing – especially for the customers.
The examples are numerous: GM Defense turned a Silverado 3500HD into an autonomous logistics truck platform, introduced a new Mongoose 8.3-liter Duramax turbo diesel on the heavy-duty models, and the all-new V8 rocks 555 hp and a mountain-moving torque of 1,230 lb-ft, with maximum towing capacity for the Silverado HD and Sierra HD now climbing to 38k pounds.
Of course, the prices also rose accordingly: the 2027 Chevy Silverado HD climbs by up to $1,500 pr trim, and the killer 8.3L Duramax alone adds $11,400 before any fees. Of course, many customers will actually focus on the regular 1500 versions because there are all-new fifth and sixth generations for the Silverado and Sierra , which come with revised design and all-new interiors plus a duet of brand-new 5.7-liter and 6.6-liter V8s to replace the lower-displacement predecessors.
There’s a lot to love about the new trucks – the new user interface inside the trucks even continues to support smartphone mirroring and allow Apple CarPlay and Android Auto to alleviate one of the biggest controversies GM has kicked off on some of its models with its users. But some folks just can’t be bothered with the modern trends – and all they see is the older trucks.
One of them is also a member of the imaginative guild of digital car content creators dwelling across the parallel universes of vehicular CGI - Abimelec Arellano, a virtual artist better known as " abimelecdesign " on social media, has prepared the newest wishful-thinking project - a cool Chevy truck, and an older one of the GMT800 variety, aka the ‘cat-eye’ model.
The pixel master is no stranger to these creations – he recently worked on the current XK70 Toyota Tundra to make it a tasty Single Cab short-bed sport truck since the automakers are keen on modern revivals of the style, like the Ford F-150 Lobo and the Ram 1500 Rumble Bee series. But now he says that he’s been thinking about the original first-gen Chevy Silverado, the GMT800 model, and its continued popularity – and an idea sprung to mind.
So, his latest unofficial, hypothetical design project is a ‘cat-eye’ Chevy Silverado GMT800 single cab short-bed truck infused with “a hefty dose of the C6 Chevrolet Corvette ZR1, one of my personal favorites of all time.” He knows the two of them weren’t contemporary (GMT800 appeared in 1999 and C6 ZR1 in late 2007), but “the styling lends itself well to the mix— especially in the front end.”
As such, he completely redesigned the front fascia as a Corvette replica adapted to the truck’s size, and the body is now also wider, “but barely noticeable.” He introduces a plethora of carbon fiber parts, a centered quad exhaust, five-lug chrome alloy wheels, side skirts, rear diffuser, and a custom interior with some Corvette parts.
Naturally, there’s also a ‘centerpiece ’: the hood offers a ‘sneak peek’ at the LS9 V8 rocking 638 hp and 604 lb-ft of torque. “I think it’s cheesy but an absolutely incredible feature at the same time,” so we dare to upgrade the situation and also dream of this blue truck getting swapped to the C8’s LT7 5.5-liter twin-turbocharged from the ZR1, complete with 1,064 horsepower!
